anya: Heads-up — turned on FP8 kernel for atlas20b on H100/L40S today for the compression bakeoff. Quick smoke shows a reproducible quality delta when model weights are aggressively structured-sparse (~65–75%). cc @sam @mike :eyes:

anya: Repro (very small):
```
# run on ded-qa harness
rw-infer --model atlas20b --quant fp8 --weights atlas20b-pruned-0.7.pt --device h100 --prompt-file small_eval.jsonl
```

anya: Metrics: eval perplexity up, some factuality hits down. Will paste numbers in a sec. Wanted to flag before wider canary.

sam: Thanks. I ran a quick eval on our MMLU subset and SQuAD-ish dev slice. Numbers (median of 3 runs):
- baseline fp16 (pruned): acc 78.9
- fp8 (pruned structured 70%): acc 75.1 (drop ~3.8pt)
- awq-8bit (post-prune): acc 78.3 (within noise)
- gptq-8bit (post-prune): acc 76.0
Perplexity: 11.9 -> 15.4 for fp8-pruned.

sam: So AWQ seems robust, pure FP8 has trouble with structured sparsity here.

mike: Hypothesis: FP8 exponent/scale estimation is getting biased by the long runs of zeros from structured pruning. The scale/amax windows are shrinking and causing clipped mantissa for rare but high-valued activations. In other words: distribution tails matter more with sparsity.

mike: Quick check I did: forcing per-channel scaling (instead of global) for the linear + attention matmul halves the delta. Suggests per-channel stats help with heterogeneous zero density.

liz: High level mitigations we should consider for the canary: 
- runtime precision override for layers with sparsity > 50% (fall back to fp16 or int8)
- use per-channel scaling + larger amax windows during inference (e.g., warmup 200 steps)
- add a simple safety gate in the model manifest: "sparsity_profile": "structured_xx"

liz: quick config example we use for canary rollout: 
```
{
  "rollout": "canary",
  "precision_overrides": {
    "dense_layers_with_sparsity_gt_50": "fp16",
    "attention_qkv": "per_channel_fp8"
  },
  "metrics_to_watch": ["mmlue_acc", "squad_f1", "per_token_logprob", "req_latency_p95"]
}
```

raj: I'll schedule a 5% traffic canary with fallback policy to AWQ for failing models. We'll log per-route deltas and set an automated rollback if mmlue_acc drops >1.5pt or per-token logprob drops >0.08.

deepbench-bot: quick-results: atlas20b-pruned-0.7 FP8 run on h100-rt-3: avg latency +4% vs fp16, memory -22%.

anya: Good. Important: we need to capture sampling tails — long prompts and few-shot examples amplify the delta (we saw one test where a 4-shot chain of thought produced hallucinated facts). Please add a small prompt-suite to the canary.

mike: Also note this is not purely a kernel bug. Quantization-aware pruning during training (keep some dense heads or retrain scale parameters) reduces the effect. For short-term, runtime gating + per-channel scaling seems lowest-risk.

sam: Action items:
- mike: prototype per-channel scaling toggle and amax-window extension (ETA EOD)
- liz: add manifest gate and canary config (ETA tomorrow)
- raj: start 5% canary once mike's toggle lands, wire alerts for the thresholds
- anya: curate a 20-prompt smoke suite with long-context items and reasoning chains (ETA EOD)

deploy-bot: Canary started (rollout_id=r-2026-3754321000, split=5%, fallback=awq-8bit).

anya: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after canary results. If anyone hits a quick root cause (kernel, scale estimator, or manifest mismatch) drop notes here before the all-hands. :thumbsup:
